rows.subtype: Approach: working backward from the target employer [Thinking]
rows.description: A student looks at what recruiters at target firms want to see, and picks two projects that show data handling and deployment instead of ten small tutorial clones.

rows.subtype: Approach: storyboarding the portfolio site on paper [Action]
rows.description: Before coding, the student sketches the home page, project pages and contact section on paper, and decides that each project needs a problem, a role, a result and a link.

rows.subtype: Approach: perfectionism delaying launch [Pitfall]
rows.description: The student keeps redesigning the fonts and animations of the portfolio for two months and never publishes it, so no recruiter sees anything at all.

rows.subtype: Approach: asking peers and seniors to critique it [Revision]
rows.description: A senior points out that project descriptions list tools but not outcomes, so the student rewrites each with the problem, what was built and what improved.

rows.subtype: Approach: staying put and waiting to be found [Thinking]
rows.description: A girl separated from her mother at a festival market remembers the rule that lost children should stop moving, reasoning that a parent will search back along the route where they were last together.

rows.subtype: Approach: mental rehearsal of a lost-child plan made beforehand [Thinking]
rows.description: Before entering the bazaar, the family asks the child what he would do if separated, and he practises saying the plan aloud: stop, look for a shop, tell the number, do not leave the area.

rows.subtype: Approach: following the first friendly adult who offers to help [Pitfall]
rows.description: A boy panics and goes off with a kind stranger who says he knows where the mother is, and ends up farther from the meeting spot because he never checked whether the person was trustworthy.

rows.subtype: Approach: switching from wandering to staying and asking [Revision]
rows.description: After walking two lanes and not finding his family, the boy realises moving is making things worse, stops beside a chai stall and asks the owner to phone his father.

rows.subtype: Approach: using the caregiver as a tool [Action]
rows.description: A toy car stops making its noise, so a toddler carries it to father, holds it up and says "no." The caregiver is treated as the repair service.

rows.subtype: Approach: imitation [Thinking]
rows.description: A toddler has seen mother call "Dadi!" when something breaks. Now a shoe strap comes loose and the toddler shouts "Dadi" toward the next room.

rows.subtype: Approach: frustration in place [Pitfall]
rows.description: A teddy is wedged behind the sofa and a toddler screams from the spot, waiting. The caregiver hears the noise but cannot tell what is wrong, so help arrives late.

rows.subtype: Approach: leading the caregiver by hand [Revision]
rows.description: Mother says "wait a minute," so the toddler grabs her finger and pulls her to the sofa, pointing at the teddy. Bringing the adult to the problem fixes the missing message.

rows.subtype: Approach: check safety and call emergency services first [Action]
rows.description: At a road crash scene, a young bystander moves to a safe spot, checks for danger such as traffic, and calls the ambulance and police using the emergency number. Calling trained responders is the priority.

rows.subtype: Approach: stay calm and follow a simple mental checklist [Thinking]
rows.description: The person recalls a first-aid class outline: safety, call for help, do not move a seriously injured person unless there is a danger, and share only what is known. A learned checklist gives structure under stress.

rows.subtype: Approach: freeze and film the scene instead of helping [Pitfall]
rows.description: Shock and habit lead the person to record video while the injured person waits. Nobody calls for help for several minutes, showing how the bystander effect delays action.

rows.subtype: Approach: seek support and review habits afterwards [Revision]
rows.description: Shaken after the event, the person talks with family, sees a doctor for lingering symptoms, and decides to follow stricter rules on helmets, speed and night riding. Learning from the event changes future routines.

rows.subtype: Approach: make-believe rehearsal [Thinking]
rows.description: A child talks through a doctor game ahead of time, saying "You are sick, I listen to your chest, then give medicine," and acts out the first lines with a doll.

rows.subtype: Approach: simple step list [Action]
rows.description: Two children assign roles, gather props such as a toy stethoscope and a bandage, and set the clinic on the mat before starting. Set-up comes before play.

rows.subtype: Approach: rigid rules [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child insists the game must go exactly as planned and corrects the friend's every line. The friend loses interest and drifts away.

rows.subtype: Approach: adding a problem [Revision]
rows.description: The play stalls after the check-up, so a child announces, "Emergency! The baby has a fever!" A new problem in the story keeps the game going.

rows.subtype: Approach: resource and budget planning with fixed-cost-first split [Thinking]
rows.description: A new graduate with a Rs 30,000 monthly salary lists rent, food, transport and the phone bill first, then sees what remains. Working from the unavoidable costs shows how little is truly free to spend.

rows.subtype: Approach: pay-yourself-first automation using a standing instruction [Action]
rows.description: On salary day the graduate sets an auto-transfer of a fixed amount to a separate savings account and a small SIP, before spending anything. Saving becomes a default rather than a daily decision.

rows.subtype: Approach: spend freely and see what is left [Pitfall]
rows.description: A first-job employee treats the credited amount as abundant, buys a phone on EMI and eats out often, and finds the account empty by the 20th. The plan fails because no total was ever set against the month.

rows.subtype: Approach: track spending for a month, then set category limits [Revision]
rows.description: After running short, the employee notes every UPI payment for a month, sees food delivery is the largest leak, and sets a weekly cap. Evidence from real data replaces a guessed budget.
